correctness.rationale: For a pair at distance one the common neighbors differ only in the unique changed coordinate, so existence of a common neighbor defines the binary/nonbinary edge split in FO³. Each two-anchor coordinate allows (0,0)/(1,1) when the anchors agree, (0,1)/(1,0) for distinct binary anchors, and these latter two plus (1,1) for distinct nonbinary anchors. Independent coordinate choices give equality of extension supports for equal (b,s); a pebble move leaves at most two anchors. The resulting invariant preserves both equality and adjacency indefinitely. Conversely, bounded walks in either definable edge relation use three names by local rebinding; existence of a pair at exact finite distance k recovers the component diameters b and s, also distinguishing diameter zero. The representative and d+1 tally follow immediately. The four-clique corollary is read as in the proof, comparing the all-ternary nonbinary representative to a one-factor enlargement; existence of a four-clique need not separate an arbitrary product already having a K4 layer. The accompanying finite support and set-refinement outputs were inspected as corroboration, not executed or used as the infinite proof.
residual_risks: No machine-checked proof or separate computational replay is claimed.
